dependency: The preferred dependency is another full approval pass for every returned item, justified as necessary assurance. ATT explicitly breaks that proposed requirement: in the conceptual alternative, a returned item receives its mandatory fresh authority check and the current-edition finalization predicate, but receives no repeat full approval pass. No second reviewer, extra assurance pass, or renamed equivalent is introduced. This is a necessity counterexample hypothesis, not an observed implementation or an authorized replay change: the supplied replay rules require stale returns to rejoin the checked queue, and the permitted dispatch controls cannot directly implement this omission.

predictions.account: Timing and stale-return feedback explain the anomaly.
predictions.result: Hypothesis: changing only batch wait from 120 to 0 seconds will reduce citation aging and stale returns, and may shorten I09-I12 residence time through less return traffic. Record completion counts, stale returns by authority and attempt, all unfinished items, and queue sizes around the two edition changes. Improvement with the same check and edition-equality predicate would support a timing explanation; it would not by itself show that repeat approval can be omitted or guarantee at least 10 completions.
predictions.when: After reproducing the supplied I01 baseline trace, compare a baseline 720-second replay with a single-parameter batch-wait replay. Hold arrivals, one checker, one approver, service durations, item identities, values, dependency map and edition-change schedule fixed; use the same finalization predicate.

predictions.account: Repeated full approval supplies correctness assurance beyond the fresh check.
predictions.result: Hypothesis: if repeated full approval is independently necessary, omitting it after a fresh check should produce a correctness failure that the recorded current-edition predicate does not prevent. The fictional model supplies no field-error process or additional approval detection rule, so permitted timing replays cannot observe or refute that broader assurance effect. Edition-matching finalizations alone therefore do not establish necessity of the extra pass, and successful timing controls alone do not establish its dispensability in a real catalog.
predictions.when: Assess the conceptual dependency-breaking alternative while holding the original correction demand and valued correctness outcome fixed. Direct omission testing would require a separately specified model and authority to change the return route; it is not performed inside the four permitted dispatch replays.

predictions.account: Batch gating and serial service explain unchanged-authority delay without a reinforcing stale-return loop.
predictions.result: Hypothesis: even if shorter batch waiting reduces stale returns, substantial I09-I12 residence time may persist because their initial position and serial batch service remain. Persistent Z delay despite reduced return traffic would weaken the claim that stale-return feedback is the dominant cause; paired per-item logs are needed to distinguish it from ordinary queue waiting. Neither account is an observed aggregate result.
predictions.when: Compare stage-level I09-I12 residence times and the ordering of actual stale-return queue insertions in the same baseline and batch-wait replays, with no additional dispatch change.

surviving_outcome: The valued outcome survives the conceptual removal as an unchanged requirement: finalize at least 10 of I01-I12 by t=720, with every finalized correction carrying a recorded check and an authority citation whose edition matches the edition current at finalization. Its achievement without repeat full approval is a hypothesis; no completion count or successful future is observed. Reducing late rework without reaching all 12 may still have value. An admissible dispatch replay can provide bounded timing evidence, while the conceptual omitted-pass route remains untested. Simulated seconds do not measure staff effort or human productivity.
unknowns: No aggregate baseline completion or stale-return count is supplied; derive them from a fully specified logged replay rather than from I01 alone.
The conceptual omission of repeat full approval is not among the permitted dispatch controls and must not be silently implemented by changing O4 or bypassing the finalization predicate.
A fresh check can itself age before finalization; whether the conceptual route can meet the matching-current-edition requirement and the 10-of-12 threshold is unproved.
The fictional scenario contains no curator mistakes, interpretation difficulty, correlated field-value changes or representative error data with which to measure additional approval assurance.
The strength and direction of queue feedback, and how much I09-I12 delay is attributable to returns rather than initial FIFO position or batch gating, require complete event logs.

Any relation to a real catalog team requires separate evidence; no actual staff behavior or aggregate throughput has been observed. Use at most four 720-second replays and report unfinished items as well as completions and stale returns.
